newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures open lower on jobless claim drop.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures open lower on jobless claim drop.

text.p: U.S. debt futures opened lower under technical pressure and extended losses after the Labor Department said initial jobless claims fell substantially in the latest week.
Jobless claims fell by 14,000 to 332,000 in the week ended June 21. Economists had predicted claims of 340,000.
"Obviously, the labor market continues to be strong," said a bond futures trader for a U.S. dealer firm, citing the report as the catalyst for the early pullback.
Traders said a "sell rallies" mentality was taking hold as technical strength waned.
"Technically the market seems to have turned the corner," said the bond trader.

The late sell-off of the previous day, triggered by rumors of large cash Treasury sales and a negative interpretation of comments from Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin that revisited the specter of concerted selling in the Treasury market, set the stage for this morning's weakness, bond traders said.

Wednesday's close below 112-02, the low from June 20 in September bond futures, confirmed the contract is on a retracement path, said a brokerage trader. The market hit a four-month peak of 112-24 on June 20.
"The move up was a sharp one, and it looks like some back and fill action is in order," the trader said.
He also linked the selling back to this week's two- and five-year note sales.
"Dealers have some supply on their hands, and a distribution trade seems reasonable," he said.
September bond futures this morning slid through support at 111-17, a double bottom from last week, trading down to 110-10 before declines stalled.
Traders said news the APICS business outlook fell to 52.4 in June from 53.0 last month was only mildly supportive.
"It helped cushion the market after the jobs number, but it was only fleeting," said a Eurodollar trader for a U.S. bank.
But a decline in the Conference Board's help wanted advertising index, which fell 6 points in May to 81.0, did help stem the slide, traders said.
September bond futures were 5/32 lower at 111-18, with September Treasury note futures down 4/32 at 108-07 and December Eurodollars down 0.005 point at 93.94.
